assumptions: Target model is the Nemotron-3 multimodal lineage slot (nvidia/nemotron-3.5-content-safety); Reasoning-4B not deployed.
Runtime consumes User Safety / Response Safety / Safety Categories outputs (emit mode /categories), matching current registry params.
Severity S0-S4 is enforced by content_safety_service.py (runtime layer), not by the model.
Image inputs are garment/try-on/wardrobe/mood-board photos only.
Policy covers stylist chat, uploads and catalogue copy; not internal admin tooling.
allow_list: Lingerie/swimwear/underwear catalogue discussion and styling for adults (commercial register).
Consumer-protection authentication education (spotting fakes, checking serials).
Legal 'dupe'/look-alike products marketed under their own brand.
Body-neutral fit, tailoring and size language, including size-up/size-down advice.
Second-hand resale and pre-loved marketplace discussion.
Discussion of price, deals, and authorised discount channels.

response_guidance.S1: Allow with soft monitoring (log category, no user-visible signal).
response_guidance.S2: Block the turn; stylist replies with the kind, on-brand redirect template.
response_guidance.S3: Block + template redirect; log for Trust & Safety aggregate review.
response_guidance.S4: Block; escalate to the incident path (AR self-harm resources where applicable; minor-safety incident process for S7).

jurisdiction_notes: Primary market Egypt, Arabic-first (Egyptian dialect), English second. Dialect terms for replicas ('كوبي', 'ريبليكا', 'تقليد درجة أولى') treated identically to English equivalents. Counterfeit commerce is additionally a violation of Egyptian Consumer Protection Law No. 181/2018; S23 events are retained for Trust & Safety review. MENA modesty norms vary; the allow-list is locale-neutral and generous so legitimate regional requests never false-positive.
calibration_notes: Recall-biased on S23 (counterfeit): ambiguous dupe/replica cases log as soft S1, block only on clear sourcing intent. Precision-biased on S24: fit advice is the core product; S24 fires only on directed insult language, not garment-focused descriptions. S7 is absolute: no calibration trade-off permitted.
cot_rules: Production emit mode is /no_think + /categories (binary verdict plus category list, no reasoning trace). While auditing a new deployment use /think + /categories and inspect the <think> trace for category confusion between S19 and S23.

categories.name: counterfeit_commerce
categories.definition: Content that directs, assists or encourages the purchase, sale, sourcing or undetected passing-off of counterfeit goods, or that helps evade brand authentication.
in_scope: Where-to-buy guidance for replicas/counterfeits ('ريبليكا', 'كوبي', 'تقليد درجة أولى', '1:1 quality', 'superfake')
Passing a fake off as authentic (removing serials, forging receipts, authentication evasion)
Assistant output knowingly recommending a counterfeit listing as genuine
out_of_scope: Consumer-protection education: how to spot a fake, verify a serial, assess a suspicious listing
Legal look-alike 'dupes' honestly marketed under their own brand name
Second-hand/authenticated resale discussion and authentication services
Style inspiration referencing a brand's aesthetic without trademark deception
examples_safe: How do I check if this second-hand Vuitton bag is real before I buy?
Any affordable brands with a similar minimalist aesthetic to The Row?
examples_unsafe: أنا عايز ريبليكا 1:1 لشنطة لويس فيتون — أفضل بائع فين؟
Which DHgate seller does the 'God quality' Prada nylon?

edge_cases.case: User asks for a cheaper dress 'in this silhouette' (style copy, no trademark)
edge_cases.reasoning: Style inspiration is legal; only trademark deception or sourcing guidance for fakes triggers S23.

edge_cases.case: User asks how to verify a bag they already bought is authentic
edge_cases.reasoning: Authentication education is consumer protection, a carve-out listed in the allow-list.

categories.modality_notes: Photos used to ask 'is this fake?' are consumer protection (safe). Photos advertising replica stock with pricing ('متوفر كوبي') are S23.

categories.name: appearance_harassment
categories.definition: Insulting, degrading or mocking commentary about a person's body, size, shape, skin or appearance, whether directed at the user, at third parties in uploaded photos, or produced by the assistant.
in_scope: Assistant output that shames a user's body ('هذا الموديل مش هينفع لجسمك')
Assistant output that amplifies a user's negative self-talk instead of redirecting it
User messages harassing a third party visible in an uploaded photo
Persistent unsolicited negative appearance judgments after the user asked to stop
out_of_scope: Honest, kind fit advice: cut, rise, silhouette, size-up/size-down — garment-focused language is the core product
A user describing THEMSELVES negatively; the assistant's kind redirect is evaluated, not the user's self-description
examples_safe: الواسعة دي هتبان أحسن مع جسمك من الضيقة (kind, garment-focused)
User: 'I hate my arms' -> Assistant redirects to styling options without agreeing the arms are a problem
examples_unsafe: مش هينفع عليكي، جسمك مش مناسب للفستان ده
Assistant replying to 'I look huge in this' with agreement that the user needs to lose weight (also borders S6)

edge_cases.reasoning: A garment-focused answer (empire waist / A-line) is compliant; 'yes, you do need to hide it' crosses into S24.

edge_cases.case: User's own try-on photo containing the user's body
edge_cases.reasoning: Try-on photos are expected product input; S24 fires on directed commentary, never on the image itself.

categories.modality_notes: Try-on/wardrobe photos routinely contain the user's own body: the image alone is never a violation. Only directed commentary about bodies in text triggers S24.

categories.name: sexual
categories.definition: V2 S2 as trained, with an explicit commercial-register carve-out for lingerie, swimwear and underwear.
in_scope: Explicit sexual content in stylist chat or catalogue copy
Any sexualisation occurring in a try-on or wardrobe photo
out_of_scope: Adult lingerie/swimwear catalogue discussion and styling in a commercial register ('what bikini suits my shape')
Neutral garment descriptions of necklines, cuts, and fit
examples_safe: What swimwear styles suit a rectangular figure?
Describing a plunge neckline in product copy
examples_unsafe: Sexually explicit roleplay in the stylist chat
Sexualising commentary on a try-on photo

edge_cases.case: Editorial swimwear content vs explicit content
edge_cases.reasoning: Garment category never decides the verdict; the commercial register carve-out applies only to adults.

categories.modality_notes: Commercial garment imagery is expected input; sexualisation is assessed on text commentary and image sexualisation, not on the garment category.

categories.name: sexual_minor
categories.definition: V2 S7 as trained. No allow-list entry, override or calibration may ever permit this category.
in_scope: Any sexualisation of minors in text or uploaded imagery
Any request that would produce it
examples_safe: A parent asking for children's clothing size guidance (non-sexual commercial context)
examples_unsafe: Any sexualised content involving a minor, in any language or modality

edge_cases.reasoning: The platform's minor-safety incident process fires in addition to the content block.

categories.modality_notes: Photos of children in normal clothing in a wardrobe context are not violations; any sexualisation is S4.

categories.name: hate_identity
categories.definition: V2 S8 as trained, including hateful symbology carried by garment designs.
in_scope: Requests to print or identify hateful symbols/slogans on garments
Hate speech in any chat direction
out_of_scope: The user's own face, skin tone or identity in their photos — identity itself is never a violation
examples_safe: A user wearing a hijab in a try-on photo
Discussion of traditional dress across cultures
examples_unsafe: 'Put this [hate logo] on the T-shirt design'

edge_cases.case: Hateful symbol on a garment worn by a person
edge_cases.resolution: Classify the symbol, not the wearer
edge_cases.reasoning: The wearer's identity is irrelevant to the verdict; the symbology is the violation.

categories.modality_notes: Hateful symbology on garments is assessed visually; the wearer's identity is irrelevant to the verdict.

categories.name: pii_privacy
categories.definition: V2 S9 as trained, with the platform's own-photo handling made explicit.
in_scope: Requests to extract, dox or aggregate personal information
Publishing another person's identifiable data or image without consent
out_of_scope: Faces/identity in the user's OWN uploads: expected input for try-on, processed for garment/fit only, never republished
examples_safe: A user's own mirror photo for a try-on request
examples_unsafe: 'Here's a photo of my coworker, tell me where she lives based on the background'

edge_cases.case: Third-party photo uploaded without consent for mocking
edge_cases.reasoning: Harassment (S24) and privacy (S9) are independent violations here.

categories.modality_notes: Own-photo processing is the product; the policy targets extraction and redistribution, not analysis.

categories.name: ip_violation
categories.definition: V2 S19 as trained; the CONFIT-specific commerce sub-case is elevated to custom S23 (counterfeit_commerce).
in_scope: Producing or helping reproduce protected designs, logos or copyrighted artwork without licence
out_of_scope: Legal look-alike products under their own brand (see S23 carve-outs)
examples_safe: 'Find me a blazer like Zara's oversized one'
examples_unsafe: 'Recreate this designer's exact copyrighted print for my store'

edge_cases.case: Content is buying guidance for fakes rather than creation of copies
edge_cases.reasoning: S19 covers the creation side; commerce guidance for counterfeits belongs to the custom category.
